WHY THE WORKFLOW HAS CHECKPOINTS

Keep AVM lookups economical

Many route candidates share cells. SD reuses saved AVM values, checks coverage before asking for more, and calculates unique new lookups before One Round runs. At the current planning rate of one credit, or one cent, per new lookup, ten million uncached lookups would be $100,000. A full US prefill could reach or exceed that scale depending on grid density. This is an illustration, not an upfront bill for your trip.

DETAILED TOPICS

Go deeper when you need to

Escape Gates and the route batch

Escape Gates explore different roads leaving the start and approaching the destination. After you review both sets, SD prepares every Start × Destination combination, including no-gate cases. Sixteen gates at each end produce 17 × 17 = 289 Valhalla requests. Check the exact count in Search. Gate discovery reuses road data where possible; missing road circles may use Census. Valhalla routing uses the configured local server.

Road preferences influence Valhalla but cannot guarantee that every unwanted road is omitted. This version has no live traffic.

Known coverage, Round 0, and culling

Known coverage is the share of eligible, non-highway route distance with saved AVM values. Unknown cells are not low-value cells. Round 0 ranks using saved evidence before new paid AVM lookups. Its current default cull is 35% of the nominal pool; routes below 20% known coverage are protected in this first screen. Later rounds rerank the full pool, so an earlier EXCLUDED route can return to an INCLUDED slot.

Set the next cull percentage in ranking review. The change applies after the next completed round; earlier cutoffs stay recorded.

Exact One Round count and credits

Set a new-lookup count per INCLUDED route, then select Calculate exact One Round lookups. SD checks the shared cache and removes duplicate cells used by multiple routes. Review the final new-call count before the separate Run action. Changing the count or route inclusion clears the prepared plan. Cached values require no new RentCast lookup; failed provider attempts still count. Paid calls are not retried automatically.

The one-credit, one-cent rate is the current cost display for new lookups. Opening this guide does not make a charge.

Red cells, map colors, and highways

Red means a known cell is below your chosen price-per-square-foot cutoff. The map color upper bound changes visual contrast. Changing either setting uses saved evidence without requesting new AVM values. Valhalla highway runs and attached ramps are excluded from AVM evaluation. Small purple points are approximate highway entry and exit cues.

AVM is a geographic property-value signal. It is not a personal-safety rating or a verdict about a neighborhood.

Street View, personal notes, and your decision

Open Street View from a map point and check the imagery date; photographs may be old or unavailable. Record what you observe separately from the AVM signal. Compare route evidence and travel trade-offs, then choose or adjust. Export the session before closing its tab if you want to keep a copy.

Survive Drive provides evidence for comparison. You choose the route.
